primary_source.title: Is This LLM Library Learning? Evaluation Must Account For Compute and Behaviour

verified: Table 3 reports GPT-4o LEGO-Prover 29.3±3.1% at $125.4 average cost, Draft-Sketch-Prove 23.1±1.2% at $22.9, and compute-corrected/reduced LEGO-Prover 23.8±1.2% at $22.6.
Table 3 reports GPT-4o-mini LEGO-Prover 25.8±1.6% at $69.9, Draft-Sketch-Prove 35.9±0.9% at $12.1, and compute-corrected/reduced LEGO-Prover 17.5±0.9% at $11.9.

For Llama3.1, the paper preserves iterative refinement and same-problem EVOLVER/PROVER use while preventing lemma sharing between problems; the no-cross-problem-sharing variant reaches 30.9±1.3% over three runs versus 29.0±2.1% non-ablated LEGO-Prover.
Within that tested Llama3.1/miniF2F/Isabelle setup, the observed advantage over Draft-Sketch-Prove is not attributable to cross-problem lemma reuse.
scope: This is a system/model/dataset-specific causal ablation, not evidence that cross-problem lemma reuse is generally useless.
The result distinguishes library/reuse behaviour from extra compute; it does not by itself establish the best memory architecture for Lean or other provers.
The paper's broader behavioural conclusions should not be transferred beyond the exact systems and analyses reported.

primary_source.title: Discovering New Theorems via LLMs with In-Context Proof Learning in Lean

verified: The controlled re-proving experiment proves 2106/2123 (99%) generated theorems with the previously generated library in context versus 1935/2123 (91%) with definitions only; the paper reports McNemar p=4×10^-35.
For the alpha-open-intersection target, 5 successful contexts × 16 attempts gives 80 with-library attempts; 7 succeed, while 0/80 without the generated library succeed.

The paper states that the generated proof for that highlighted target does not use other generated theorems as lemmas, supporting an in-context proof-strategy channel separate from direct lemma invocation.
scope: The context intervention changes prompt content and is not matched for context tokens or total compute, so the experiment identifies a benefit of the broader generated-library context package rather than a minimal isolated memory mechanism.
The 7/80 versus 0/80 result is for one target theorem and must not be generalized as a universal effect size.
The aggregate 99% versus 91% experiment can mix direct theorem availability with strategy guidance; only the highlighted target is explicitly shown not to invoke generated theorems as lemmas.
The paper itself lists the focus on a single target theorem for the alpha-open analysis as a limitation.

combined_interpretation: The two primary sources jointly support a strict evaluation separation: prior verified proof/library context can improve later proving through a guidance channel, yet apparent library gains can disappear under compute correction and, in one LEGO-Prover ablation, cross-problem lemma sharing is not the cause. Therefore direct reusable-lemma value, advisory-context value, and extra-compute value should be measured separately rather than inferred from library presence alone.
